messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stacy Liu <stacy.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Acme MAP Weekly: evaluation progress + priority SLA ask

Team — looping everyone in for this week’s MAP checkpoint with Acme. High-level: Acme’s security review is moving faster than expected but they’ve flagged an uptime SLA clause tied to production pilots; procurement wants a definitive timeline for go/no-go by 11/10 so they can close the quarter. Stacy asked me to surface whether we can commit to a short-term priority support window while the Dedicated capacity is provisioned.

Summary (current):
- PoC infra: staging cluster ready; initial load tests ran 10/29 and 10/30 — 95th percentile latency at target for 512-token loads.
- Security: SOC-2 artifacts delivered 10/28; Acme asked for audit log retention detail (see MAP action item #3).
- Cost eval: projected token unit economics look within their target by using quantized model variant; finance asked for expanded example traffic in MAP doc.

Open items + owners (for this week):
1) Priority support / SLA exception request — owner: Rafael Mendes — action: propose short-term SLA commitment (2-week elevated support window) and support staffing plan.
2) Audit log retention spec — owner: Marissa Cole — action: confirm retention window and sample audit logs.
3) Finalized eval dataset & throughput profile — owner: Karthik Iyer — action: provide representative production traffic by 11/04.
4) Contract redlines (procurement) — owner: Sean Gallagher — action: confirm any nonstandard SLAs they will insist on.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick sync today (30 min) if possible to confirm support coverage and draft SLA text. I can propose the elevated-support wording for a two-week pilot and include on-call contacts.
- Share MAP_rev2.xlsx (updated timeline & owners) after this sync.

Stacy — can you confirm if procurement needs a signed commitment (DocuSign) to keep the 11/10 close window, or is an emailed exec sponsor commitment sufficient for now?

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Acme MAP Weekly: evaluation progress + priority SLA ask

Rafael / team — thanks for the update. Short answer: procurement needs a stated SLA posture from Redwood to keep the deal moving; an emailed exec sponsor note will help for now but procurement expects formal language before 11/10. We’re not asking for a permanent SLA change — just a time-bound priority support commitment that guarantees escalation to an exec on our side and a named Redwood on-call contact within 30 minutes for Severity 1.

To be concrete: we need the following by COB 11/03 to avoid procurement pause:
- A one-page commitment (PDF/DocuSign) that outlines the 2-week elevated support window starting on provisioning, named contacts, and a fallback plan if the dedicated capacity rollout slips.
- Confirmation that Redwood will prioritize any critical remediation for the pilot environment within the agreed window.

I’m happy to be the exec sponsor on our end but procurement will want a Redwood exec or VP-level assurance in the doc. Can you flag whether Sean or Rafael can sign that commitment?

Stacy
Stacy Liu
Head of AI Integrations — Acme Corp
stacy.liu@acme.com

Stacy / Rafael / team — we can support the requested temporary SLA commitment. Below is the operational proposal I discussed with the Infra on-call leads this morning. I’m attaching MAP_rev2.xlsx (timeline + owners) to this thread.

Operational proposal (temporary, 2-week pilot):
- Priority window: first 2 weeks post-dedicated-provisioning or as requested by Acme; Redwood will designate one named on-call (primary) and one backup. Primary on-call: Hiro Tanaka (hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai), backup: Marissa Cole.
- Severity definitions & RTO: S1 (platform down) — acknowledge within 30 minutes, remediation comms within 2 hours; S2 (severe degradation) — acknowledge within 60 minutes, mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- Exec escalation: if S1 incident is unresolved after 6 hours, the Redwood VP of Ops will engage (we’d propose Matt Chen or equivalent; will confirm title/availability for the DocuSign).
- Fallback: if dedicated capacity rollout slips, we provide a temporary hosted fallback with the same priority handling for the pilot duration.

Attachments: MAP_rev2.xlsx (see tab 'SLA_proposal' for exact text we can convert into a 1-page DocuSign).

Requested actions (by 11/03):
- Rafael / Sean: confirm who will be the Redwood signatory for the 1-page DocuSign.
- Karthik: share the production traffic sample by 11/04 per the MAP so we can validate the fallback capacity numbers.
- Stacy: confirm if Acme legal needs additional language around indemnity (we can flag but prefer to avoid broad changes for a time-bound pilot).

I’ll draft the 1-page commitment and circulate for signature once signatory is confirmed.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
